```python
class Computer:
    """Complex product to build"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.cpu = None
        self.ram = None
        self.storage = None
        self.gpu = None
        self.os = None
    
    def __str__(self):
        specs = [
            "💻 Computer Specifications:",
            f"   CPU: {self.cpu}",
            f"   RAM: {self.ram}",
            f"   Storage: {self.storage}",
            f"   GPU: {self.gpu}",
            f"   OS: {self.os}"
        ]
        return "\n".join(specs)

class ComputerBuilder:
    """Builder for constructing Computer"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.computer = Computer()
    
    def set_cpu(self, cpu):
        self.computer.cpu = cpu
        return self  # Return self for chaining
    
    def set_ram(self, ram):
        self.computer.ram = ram
        return self
    
    def set_storage(self, storage):
        self.computer.storage = storage
        return self
    
    def set_gpu(self, gpu):
        self.computer.gpu = gpu
        return self
    
    def set_os(self, os):
        self.computer.os = os
        return self
    
    def build(self):
        return self.computer

# Director classes for common configurations
class GamingComputerBuilder:
    """Build a gaming computer with preset specs"""
    @staticmethod
    def build():
        return ComputerBuilder()\
            .set_cpu("Intel i9-13900K")\
            .set_ram("32GB DDR5")\
            .set_storage("2TB NVMe SSD")\
            .set_gpu("NVIDIA RTX 4090")\
            .set_os("Windows 11 Pro")\
            .build()
```

Purpose: Create new objects by copying existing objects (prototypes).

Visual:
    ┌──────────────┐
    │  Prototype   │
    │──────────────│
    │ + clone()    │
    └──────┬───────┘
           │
           │ implements
    ┌──────▼───────┐
    │ConcreteClass │
    │──────────────│
    │ + clone()    │
    └──────────────┘
           │
           │ clone()
           ▼
    [New Instance] (copy of original)

Use Cases:
- When object creation is expensive
- When you need many similar objects
- When you want to avoid subclasses
- Cloning database records, game characters, documents

```python
class PizzaBuilder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pizza = Pizza()
    
    def set_size(self, size):
        self.pizza.size = size
        return self
    
    def set_crust(self, crust):
        self.pizza.crust = crust
        return self
    
    def add_cheese(self):
        self.pizza.cheese = True
        return self
    
    def add_topping(self, topping):
        self.pizza.toppings.append(topping)
        return self
    
    def build(self):
        return self.pizza

# Create custom pizza
my_pizza = PizzaBuilder()\
    .set_size("Large")\
    .set_crust("Thin Crust")\
    .add_cheese()\
    .add_topping("Pepperoni")\
    .add_topping("Mushrooms")\
    .add_topping("Olives")\
    .build()

print(my_pizza)
```

```python
class GameCharacter:
    """Base character class"""
    def __init__(self, name, health, attack, defense, skills):
        self.name = name
        self.health = health
        self.attack = attack
        self.defense = defense
        self.skills = skills.copy()  # Make a copy of list
        self.inventory = []
    
    def clone(self):
        """Create a deep copy of the character"""
        return deepcopy(self)
    
    def __str__(self):
        return f"""
    🎮 {self.name}
       HP: {self.health} | ATK: {self.attack} | DEF: {self.defense}
       Skills: {', '.join(self.skills)}
       Inventory: {', '.join(self.inventory) if self.inventory else 'Empty'}
    """.strip()

# Create prototype characters
print("\n🔍 Testing Prototype Pattern:")
print("\n1. Creating prototype warrior:")
warrior_prototype = GameCharacter(
    name="Warrior",
    health=150,
    attack=50,
    defense=40,
    skills=["Slash", "Block", "Charge"]
)
print(warrior_prototype)

print("\n2. Cloning warriors for an army:")
warriors = []
for i in range(3):
    warrior = warrior_prototype.clone()
    warrior.name = f"Warrior #{i+1}"
    warrior.inventory = [f"Sword {i+1}", "Shield"]
    warriors.append(warrior)
    print(warrior)

print("\n3. Modifying clone doesn't affect prototype:")
warriors[0].health = 100
warriors[0].skills.append("Berserk")
print(f"\nPrototype health: {warrior_prototype.health}")
print(f"Clone health: {warriors[0].health}")
print(f"Prototype skills: {warrior_prototype.skills}")
print(f"Clone skills: {warriors[0].skills}")

print("\n\n📄 Another Example - Document Templates:")
```

```python
class Document:
    def __init__(self, title, content, author):
        self.title = title
        self.content = content
        self.author = author
        self.metadata = {}
    
    def clone(self):
        return deepcopy(self)
    
    def __str__(self):
        return f"""
📄 Document: {self.title}
   Author: {self.author}
   Content: {self.content[:50]}...
   Metadata: {self.metadata}
        """.strip()

# Create template
template = Document(
    title="Monthly Report Template",
    content="This is a standard monthly report template with predefined sections...",
    author="Company"
)
template.metadata = {"type": "report", "department": ""}

print("\nTemplate:")
print(template)

# Clone for different departments
print("\nCreating reports from template:")
sales_report = template.clone()
sales_report.title = "Sales Report - January"
sales_report.author = "John Doe"
sales_report.metadata["department"] = "Sales"
print(sales_report)

engineering_report = template.clone()
engineering_report.title = "Engineering Report - January"
engineering_report.author = "Jane Smith"
engineering_report.metadata["department"] = "Engineering"
print(engineering_report)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ABSTRACT FACTORY PATTERN
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("5️⃣  ABSTRACT FACTORY PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Purpose: Create families of related objects without specifying concrete classes.

Visual:
                ┌─────────────────┐
                │AbstractFactory  │
                │─────────────────│
                │+ createButton() │
                │+ createCheckbox()│
                └────────┬────────┘
                         │
           ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
           │                           │
    ┌──────▼──────┐            ┌──────▼──────┐
    │WindowsFactory│            │ MacFactory  │
    │──────────────│            │─────────────│
    │+ create...() │            │+ create...()│
    └──────┬───────┘            └──────┬──────┘
           │                           │
      Creates ├──────┐            Creates ├──────┐
              │      │                    │      │
         ┌────▼─┐ ┌──▼───┐          ┌────▼─┐ ┌──▼───┐
         │WinBtn│ │WinChk│          │MacBtn│ │MacChk│
         └──────┘ └──────┘          └──────┘ └──────┘

Use Cases:
- UI components for different platforms
- Database drivers for different databases
- Cross-platform applications
""")
```

class Application
sections.body:
Purpose: Allow incompatible interfaces to work together. Convert interface of class into another interface.

Visual:
    Client ──► Target Interface
                      ▲
                      │ implements
                 ┌────┴─────┐
                 │  Adapter  │
                 │───────────│
                 │ adapts    │
                 └─────┬─────┘
                       │ uses
                       ▼
                  Adaptee
                  (incompatible interface)

Real Example - Power Adapter:
    US Plug (110V) ──► Adapter ──► EU Socket (220V)

Use Cases:
- Integrating legacy code with new systems
- Using third-party libraries with different interfaces
- Making incompatible classes work together

```python
# Client code
class Application:
    def __init__(self, factory: GUIFactory):
        self.factory = factory
        self.button = factory.create_button()
        self.checkbox = factory.create_checkbox()
    
    def render_ui(self):
        print(self.button.render())
        print(self.checkbox.render())
    
    def interact(self):
        print(self.button.click())
        print(self.checkbox.toggle())
        print(self.checkbox.toggle())

# Demo
print("\n🔍 Testing Abstract Factory Pattern:")

import platform
current_os = platform.system()

print("\n1. Creating UI for Windows:")
windows_factory = WindowsFactory()
windows_app = Application(windows_factory)
windows_app.render_ui()
windows_app.interact()

print("\n2. Creating UI for Mac:")
mac_factory = MacFactory()
mac_app = Application(mac_factory)
mac_app.render_ui()
mac_app.interact()

print("\n3. Creating UI for Linux:")
linux_factory = LinuxFactory()
linux_app = Application(linux_factory)
linux_app.render_ui()
linux_app.interact()

print(f"\n✨ Current OS: {current_os} - Factory pattern allows platform-specific UI!")

# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================

print("🏛️  STRUCTURAL DESIGN PATTERNS")
print("=" * 80)
```
